The table has 17 rows: 16 for “Uranium, U content” and 1 for “Rare earth elements, recovered from uranium-ore residue”. NAC Kazatomprom JSC is named as an owner in 16 of the 17 rows; its stated shares range from 30% to 100%. Uranium One Inc. is named as an owner in 2 of the 17 rows; its stated shares range from 20% to 50%.

All facility details, locations, and owners appear in the table below, sourced from the [USGS Minerals Yearbook, volume III (Area Reports: International), country chapters](https://pubs.usgs.gov/myb/vol3/2023/myb3-2023-kazakhstan.pdf) (2023 chapter on [/world/kz](/world/kz)). The capacity figure "24000 metric tons" is printed once for the uranium mining operations together, and capacity is capacity, not production.

Kazakhstan's mine production is 23,270 t, which represents a 38.6% world share of total global production of 60,213 t in 2024, ranking 1 globally, according to the [WNA, World Nuclear Association, World Uranium Mining Production, updated 2026-10-09: Uranium](https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/nuclear-fuel-cycle/mining-of-uranium/world-uranium-mining-production) on the [Uranium](/resources/uranium) page (status: Sourced).

The buyers of Kazakhstan's uranium output are not in our sources. A source that would settle it: offtake and supply agreements disclosed in the producers' annual reports and filings, customs and trade records (UN Comtrade), and the buyers' own procurement disclosures.

Outside the corpus — Kazatomprom and its operating joint ventures sell uranium under bilateral supply contracts to electric power utilities and nuclear fuel cycle companies across North America, Europe, and East Asia, or deliver unrefined product to partner-owned conversion and fuel fabrication facilities abroad.
